column1: # Hardcore Nuzlocke level caps for the vanilla Gen 3 games (2026-09-29).
# A cap is the level of the highest-level Pokemon on the boss's team in the first-run fight. Rematches are left out.
# That is the definition Bulbapedia gives for the Hardcore "Level Cap" rule and the one Nuzlocke University uses.
# Source: docs/research/nuzlocke-gen1-3.md sections 6.1 (Ruby and Sapphire), 7.1 (Emerald) and 8.1 (FireRed and
# LeafGreen). Each number was computed from the pret disassemblies (pokeruby, pokeemerald, pokefirered: trainer
# tables and trainer parties) and checked against Bulbapedia's trainer pages, Nuzlocke University's Hardcore level
# cap page and Serebii. Two community datasets that disagree (Drake 54, Lt. Surge 45) are wrong and are not used.
# NuzlockeRomCapsTest reads the same numbers back out of clean dumps when they are on hand.
# These are the FALLBACK. When the tracker can read the trainer data out of the loaded ROM it uses the boss's real
# party levels instead, which is what a randomized or Kaizo-scaled game needs (NuzlockeCaps, GbaTracker.levelCaps).
# game: rs = Ruby and Sapphire, e = Emerald, frlg = FireRed and LeafGreen.
# key: gymN is the Nth badge (the tracker reads badges as bits, badge N = bit N-1); e4-N is the Nth Elite Four
# member; champion; post is a fight after the Hall of Fame.
# ids: the boss's trainer ids, comma separated (FireRed and LeafGreen's Champion has one per rival starter).
